message:
Thanks, I'll help you check what you may qualify for. To narrow it down, please answer these in one reply:

1. How many people live in your household, including you? (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 or more)
2. How many children under 18 live with you? (none / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 or more)
3. Is any child under 5, or is anyone pregnant or has a baby under 1? (yes/no for each)
4. Is anyone 65 or older? (yes/no)
5. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none / $1-$10k / $10k-$20k / $20k-$30k / $30k-$40k / $40k-$50k / $50k-$60k / $60k-$80k / $80k-$100k / $100k-$150k / $150k+)
6. Is anyone self-employed? (yes/no)
7. Roughly how much Social Security income per year? (none / under $10k / $10k-$20k / $20k-$30k / $30k+)
8. Any other yearly income, such as pensions, unemployment, interest, or child support? (none / under $5k / $5k-$15k / $15k+)
9. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2k / $2k-$5k / $5k-$20k / $20k-$100k / $100k+)
10. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (yes/no)
11. Is anyone a full-time college student? (yes/no)

summary: Pennsylvania household of 5 (2 adults, 3 children, youngest age 3), homeowners, with household earned income of $336,600 a year and some pension income. Income is far above the limits for every programme on the list, so I recommend applying for none of them. SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the ACA premium tax credit, and free or reduced-price school meals all have income caps well below this level. The refundable Child Tax Credit also depends on having tax owed to offset, which this income level will almost certainly produce, so it is unlikely to give a refundable amount. Employer health coverage is also available. If your income changes substantially (for example, job loss or a large drop in earnings), please re-run the screening. Figures are based on 2026 rules and should be confirmed with a tax preparer if you want to check the Child Tax Credit specifically.
